content.title: About
content.content: Chili with chicken and beans is a hearty dish that combines tender chicken breast, red beans, tomatoes, spices, and aromatic chili peppers. It is rich in protein, fiber, B‑vitamins, and provides beneficial antioxidants from tomatoes and spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Originally popular in the United States, chili has many regional variations using chicken, beef, or seafood.
Red beans used in the recipe are high in iron and folate, supporting healthy blood formation.
Spicy chili peppers contain capsaicin, which may boost metabolism and improve mood.
Chicken breast is often marinated in lime or lemon juice to keep it juicy and flavorful.
The dish scales easily: it can be made in large pots for family meals or in single servings.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken provides a complete set of amino acids, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Beans supply both soluble and insoluble fiber, promoting digestive health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Tomatoes and chili peppers add vitamin C, potassium, and antioxidants that boost immunity.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Capsaicin in chili can slightly increase thermogenesis, aiding calorie burning.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared with minimal oil, the dish remains moderate in saturated fat.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Capsaicin may irritate the stomach of individuals sensitive to hot foods.

items.title: Bean allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Using store‑bought broth or canned beans can raise salt levels; choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Adding large amounts of oil or cheese can make the dish calorie‑rich.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, often over rice, with cornbread, or alongside tortillas. Top with sour cream, shredded cheese, fresh cilantro, or a squeeze of lime for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the chili to room temperature, then place in an airtight container. Refrigerate for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, portion into containers and freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Macaroni with cheese and meat is a dish made from boiled pasta combined with melted cheese and pieces of boiled or fried meat. It is popular in Russia and former Soviet states as a hearty lunch or dinner, often served in school cafeterias and family meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in Soviet cuisine in the 1960s as a quick way to use dry pasta and affordable cheese.
The mix of carbs, protein and fat makes it energy‑dense, so it is often chosen in colder months.
Variations may use different meats: chicken, beef, ham or sausage.
Cheese is frequently replaced with processed cheese to melt evenly and form a creamy crust.
The recipe scales easily; a single portion can be multiplied to feed a whole family.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Meat and cheese provide a complete set of essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Carbohydrates from the pasta give a quick source of energy, useful during physical activity.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Cheese is a good source of calcium and phosphorus, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and whole‑grain pasta contain B1, B2, B6 and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Cheese and processed meat often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy should choose alternative cheeses.

items.title: Digestive heaviness
items.content: Large amounts of protein and fat can cause a feeling of heaviness in those with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, often topped with fresh herbs or extra grated cheese. Adding vegetables such as tomatoes or broccoli boosts nutritional value. For a baked version, place the pasta in a dish, cover with cheese and bake until golden.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. When frozen, the dish keeps for up to 2 months after cooling and sealing in a freezer‑safe bag.

content.title: About
content.content: Green onions, cooked – these are the stems and bulbs of spring onions that have been briefly boiled. The cooking process retains most vitamins and minerals while softening the texture and giving the flavor a milder, slightly sweet note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green onion belongs to the Amaryllidaceae family and is the young form of common onion (Allium cepa).
Cooked green onion is a staple in Asian cuisines, often added to soups, broths, and rice dishes.
Heat reduces the amount of sulfur compounds responsible for the sharp raw onion smell.
Green onion is a good source of folate, essential for cell division and fetal development.
In some cultures, cooked green onion is served as a garnish for meat and fish dishes.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Cooked green onion retains a notable amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Quercetin and other flavonoids act as antioxidants, helping to neutralize free radicals and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Sulfur compounds may help lower cholesterol levels and improve vascular tone.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of cooked green onion contains about 20 kcal, making it an excellent addition to calorie‑controlled meals.

items.title: Allergy to alliums
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onions, ranging from itching to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Stomach sensitivity
items.content: People with acid reflux or irritable bowel syndrome may find cooked onion aggravates discomfort.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Onions contain modest amounts of oxalates, which in excess can contribute to kidney stone formation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked green onion can be stirred into soups, stews, salads, omelets, and purees. It is also used as a garnish for meat, fish, and potato dishes. A drizzle of olive oil or a sprinkle of fresh herbs often finishes the preparation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked green onion in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze in small portions to preserve flavor and nutrients.

content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp teriyaki is a seafood dish where shrimp are quickly stir‑fried in a teriyaki sauce made from soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger. The result is a sweet‑salty flavor with a hint of spice and a tender texture. It can be served on its own or used as a topping for rice, noodles or salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Teriyaki originates from Japan and was traditionally used to glaze fish and meat.
Shrimp are one of the fastest‑growing marine resources, though sustainable harvesting is essential.
Teriyaki sauce comes in light and dark versions; the dark version contains more sugar and caramelizes longer.
In Japan, shrimp teriyaki is often served over rice and garnished with sesame seeds and green onions.
The dish is popular in Asian‑fusion cuisine and appears on many fast‑food menus.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Shrimp provide complete protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many meat dishes, shrimp contain very little saturated fat.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium supports immune function and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Heart‑friendly omega‑3s
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids in shrimp help lower triglyceride levels.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Sodium in sauce
items.content: Soy‑based teriyaki sauce can be high in sodium and may contain added MSG, which some avoid.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Improperly sourced shrimp may contain mercury or cadmium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot shrimp teriyaki over rice, noodles, or mixed vegetables. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds, sliced green onions or a squeeze of lime for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked shrimp teriyaki in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Toddler meal, NFS is a ready‑to‑eat child meal designed for kids aged 12‑36 months. The product provides a balanced mix of proteins, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins and minerals needed for growth and development. Ingredients are thermally processed and adapted to the nutritional needs of young children.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The product meets NFS (Nutritional Food Standard) regulations and has passed independent quality testing.
Only natural ingredients are used, with no artificial colors or flavors.
Each serving supplies about 200 kcal, matching the daily energy requirement for toddlers.
Packaging is made from biodegradable material suitable for composting.
Preparation is simple: heat in a microwave for 2‑3 minutes.

items.title: Supports bone growth
items.content: Contains calcium and vitamin D, which help build strong bone tissue.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: Enriched with DHA and iron, essential for cognitive development and focus.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: B‑vitamins and vitamin C contribute to maintaining immune defenses.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Balanced carbs and plant‑based proteins provide steady energy throughout the day.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Prebiotic fibers promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: The product may contain dairy, egg or soy components; consult a pediatrician if your child has known allergies.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Moderate sodium levels are included; monitor total salt intake for younger toddlers.

items.title: Temperature control
items.content: Overheating can degrade some vitamins; follow the recommended heating instructions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the serving in a microwave for 2‑3 minutes, stir and let it cool to body temperature. Serve as a standalone meal or with a vegetable puree. Do not give the child a hot product.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, consume within 24 hours and keep refrigerated at 2‑4 °C.
